Temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), blood pressure is 128/74 mm Hg, pulse is 88/min, and the abdomen is distended and tympanitic with diffuse mild tenderness but no guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are hypoactive. Laboratory studies show no leukocytosis and normal serum lactate. Abdominal radiography shows diffuse dilation of both small and large bowel without a transition point. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A: Begin bowel rest, intravenous fluids, correction of electrolyte abnormalities, and early ambulation
B: Perform urgent exploratory laparotomy for suspected bowel ischemia
C: Administer neostigmine for acute colonic pseudo-obstruction
D: Obtain CT angiography to evaluate for mesenteric ischemia

stem: A 27-year-old woman comes to the clinic because of a 2-month history of recurrent episodes of sudden intense fear, palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, and a sense of impending doom. The episodes last 8–12 minutes, occur without warning (including while she is at home watching television), and are followed by persistent worry about having another attack and concern that she is “going crazy.” She has begun to avoid leaving the house alone. Physical examination, ECG, and laboratory studies (including TSH) are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A: Generalized anxiety disorder
D: Specific phobia

stem: A 54-year-old man undergoes colonoscopy after a positive fecal immunochemical test obtained during routine colorectal cancer screening. He has no abdominal pain, weight loss, or change in bowel habits. Colonoscopy reveals a 4-cm ulcerated rectal mass with its lower edge 6 cm from the anal verge; the remainder of the colon is normal. Biopsy shows moderately differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma. Digital rectal examination reveals a firm mass with reduced mobility. CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis show no distant metastases. Which of the following is the most appropriate next study to assess local tumor extent and guide neoadjuvant treatment and surgical planning?
A: Whole-body fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT
C: High-resolution pelvic MRI with a rectal cancer protocol
D: Repeat colonoscopy with additional tumor biopsies

stem: A 68-year-old right-handed man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the emergency department after a 30-minute episode of left arm weakness and difficulty speaking that resolved completely. He is now asymptomatic with a normal neurologic examination. MRI of the brain shows no acute infarction. Carotid duplex ultrasound reveals 70% stenosis of the right internal carotid artery. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A: Aspirin 325 mg daily
D: Computed tomography angiography of the head and neck

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents to your office 3 months after being laid off from her job due to company restructuring. She reports feeling sad, having difficulty sleeping, and a lack of interest in activities she previously enjoyed. She denies any suicidal ideation or feelings of worthlessness. She is worried about her financial situation and is actively applying to new jobs.
A: Adjustment disorder with depressed mood
D: Posttraumatic stress disorder

stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after suddenly falling while standing at a concert. Witnesses report that he stiffened, had rhythmic jerking of all four extremities for approximately 90 seconds, and was confused and somnolent for 20 minutes afterward. He bit the lateral aspect of his tongue and had urinary incontinence. He has no prior history of seizures, takes no medications, and denies alcohol or illicit drug use. On examination, he has returned to baseline without focal neurologic deficits. Serum glucose, electrolytes, calcium, magnesium, complete blood count, and toxicology screening are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in evaluation?
A: Obtain brain MRI with an epilepsy-specific protocol and arrange outpatient electroencephalography
B: Start levetiracetam immediately without further testing
C: Perform lumbar puncture to evaluate for central nervous system infection
D: Obtain a routine noncontrast head CT only and discharge without follow-up
E: Diagnose vasovagal syncope and provide reassurance

stem: A 15-month-old boy is brought to the clinic for a routine health supervision visit. He was born at full term with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. His diet consists primarily of cow's milk (about 1 liter per day) and crackers; he refuses most solid foods. On physical examination, he appears pale and irritable. Growth parameters are at the 50th percentile for weight and length. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A: Advise limiting cow's milk intake and starting iron supplementation
B: Obtain a complete blood count and serum ferritin level
D: Refer for a dietary consultation only
E: Start a multivitamin with iron and repeat evaluation in 6 months

stem: A 32-year-old G1P0 at 34 weeks of gestation presents to the office complaining of severe pruritus that has been worsening over the past 2 weeks. She describes the itching as most intense on her palms and soles and notes that it is worse at night. She has tried topical emollients and antihistamines without relief. Physical examination reveals excoriations on the wrists and ankles but no rash, jaundice, or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory studies show a total bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase of 45 U/L, alanine aminotransferase of 52 U/L, and serum bile acids of 35 μmol/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A: Administer oral ursodeoxycholic acid
D: Schedule induction of labor at 39 weeks

stem: A 64-year-old man is evaluated on the fifth day after open sigmoid colectomy for diverticular disease. He has had a temperature of 38.6°C (101.5°F) for the past 12 hours. He reports mild suprapubic discomfort and has been ambulating with assistance. An indwelling urinary catheter placed at the time of surgery was removed on postoperative day 4. His pulse is 96/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg; oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. Examination shows clear lungs, a soft abdomen with a clean, intact midline incision without erythema or drainage, and no calf tenderness. Leukocyte count is 13,200/mm3. Urinalysis shows 50 leukocytes/hpf, positive leukocyte esterase, and many bacteria. Chest radiograph shows no infiltrate. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's fever?
A: Anastomotic leak
D: Surgical site infection

stem: A 68-year-old man with a 45-pack-year smoking history and hypertension presents for a routine health maintenance visit. He has no abdominal or back pain. His blood pressure is 138/86 mm Hg, and his physical examination, including abdominal examination, is unremarkable. He has never undergone abdominal imaging. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A: One-time screening abdominal ultrasonography
D: Magnetic resonance angiography of the abdominal aorta

stem: A 34-year-old woman comes to the clinic to establish care. She reports a 9-month history of constant, diffuse abdominal pain, bloating, and severe fatigue. She has seen three different gastroenterologists and two rheumatologists over the past year. Extensive laboratory testing, abdominal imaging, and upper and lower endoscopies have shown no abnormalities. The patient says she spends several hours each night researching her symptoms online and is terrified she has an undiagnosed terminal cancer. She has missed multiple days of work due to her symptoms and anxiety. Vital signs and physical examination are unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A: Advise the patient that her symptoms are psychological in origin
B: Prescribe a trial of a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
C: Reassure the patient that her diagnostic workup is completely normal
D: Refer the patient for a comprehensive psychiatric evaluation
E: Schedule regular, brief outpatient follow-up appointments

stem: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a 2-day history of sore throat, fever to 39°C, and headache. He has no cough or rhinorrhea. Examination reveals tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy and pharyngeal erythema with tonsillar exudates. A rapid antigen detection test is positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A: Initiate amoxicillin therapy
D: Start a 5-day course of azithromycin

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with a 2-cm palpable, firm mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. Mammography shows a spiculated mass, and core needle biopsy reveals invasive ductal carcinoma, estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative. Sentinel lymph node biopsy shows no metastasis. She is otherwise healthy with no comorbidities. What is the most appropriate surgical management?
A: Breast-conserving surgery with sentinel lymph node biopsy followed by whole-breast radiation therapy
B: Modified radical mastectomy without radiation therapy
C: Total mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection
D: Breast-conserving surgery alone without radiation therapy
E: Radical mastectomy with chest wall radiation

stem: A 65-year-old man with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 4 is admitted to the hospital with a serum potassium level of 6.8 mEq/L and ECG changes consistent with hyperkalemia. He is asymptomatic and has a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in managing this patient's hyperkalemia?
A: Administer intravenous calcium gluconate
D: Prescribe oral potassium-binding resin
